Thanks for the packet, Sung — quick heads up: Hansea is a non-US entity, so we cannot accept a W-9. For our legal and tax team to complete vendor setup and issue a PO, we need: 

1) A completed W-8BEN-E (signed) rather than a W-9.
2) The English translation of your Business Registration or a government-issued certificate (KRA).
3) Confirmation of your U.S. US tax classification box (i.e., chapter 3 status) on the W-8BEN-E and whether you claim treaty benefits.

I copied Laura from Procurement — she will track the PO queue. If you can upload a signed W-8BEN-E and the translated registration, we can expedite. If you prefer, we can send a DocuSign for the W-8BEN-E.

Thanks,

Hi Sung — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the W-8BEN-E. A couple of follow-ups from tax/compliance: 

- The W-8BEN-E you provided fills the chapter 3 classification but does not include an attached official residency certificate. For our US payor obligations we need either: (a) a certificate of tax residency from the Korean tax authority (KRA) or (b) a localized government-issued business certificate that clearly states tax residency, plus a signed statement confirming no US-sourced income will be reported for this contract.
- If you claim treaty benefits on the W-8BEN-E (Part III), please include the specific article and attach supporting documentation (KRA certificate or treaty-residence attestation).
- Also: please confirm the person who signed the W-8BEN-E is authorized to sign on behalf of Hansea Tech (title and copy of signatory ID or board minutes).

If you can provide the KRA certificate (English or translated) and a brief signatory confirmation, Procurement can move the PO out of review and into issuance. We can accept the KRA as a scanned PDF; notarization is not required for the initial PO but may be requested for payment.

Laura — can you hold this in conditional queue 18 pending receipt of the KRA doc?

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Tax Counsel
